maya: Kicked off hyperparam+quantization sweep for Asteria-embed (candidate for next onboard). Quick summary: float32 baseline recall@10=0.842, int8 (QAT-ish) ~0.826, int6 PQ-style drop to 0.793. Silhouette (kmeans, k=200) fell 0.42 -> 0.31 on int6. Uploading a couple of plots: https://internal.s3/asteria/sweep/1766664321/heatmap.png :eyes:
arjun: Can you paste the eval command and which pooling you used? mean pooling over last 1 token? :thinking_face:
maya: Eval snippet below (ran on holdout-20k, recall@k/UMAP/silhouette):

```
./r_eval --model asteria-embed-v0 
        --pooling mean --normalize true 
        --quant int6-pq --pq-m 16 
        --index hnsw --M 32 --ef_construction 200 
        --holdout holdout-20k.jsonl 
        --metrics recall@1,5,10,silhouette,umap_variance
```

maya: Also tried mean+whiten (PCA whiten) as postproc and that recovered ~+3.5% relative on recall@10 for int6 (0.820).
sophie: Hmm PCA whitening helping is interesting — suggests global scale shift from quantization. Did you try L2-normalize before PQ? That often stabilizes PQ codebooks.
maya: Yup: normalize before PQ + OPQ rotation helped even more: int6 -> recall@10 0.831, silhouette 0.38. So pipeline that worked: normalize -> OPQ(32) -> PQ(m=16) -> index.
tom: Nice. How about hybrid embeddings? last4-layer-concat (dim x4) + reduce via PCA -> did you try mixing layers? Might give robustness vs quantization.
maya: Did a tiny run: concat-last4 + PCA(512) then PQ-int6 gave recall@10 0.838 (surpassed base float32 in some microcohorts). But cost/size spike is nontrivial — index size +40%.
arjun: Can we trade off index params instead? Increase ef_search (runtime) to recover recall while keeping PQ low-precision? What happens at ef_search=512?
maya: I ran ef_search sweep: ef=128 -> 0.793, ef=256 -> 0.810, ef=512 -> 0.827 on int6+OPQ+norm. So search params recover ~half of the gap. Latency at 512 is ~2.3x vs 128.
sophie: We should also check cohort-level regressions (short queries / multilingual). Any per-cohort diffs?
maya: Short queries (<= 8 tokens) degrade more: float32 recall@10 short=0.79 vs int6+OPQ 0.74 (large gap). Multilang (fr/es) shows smaller drop. I attached a small CSV: https://internal.s3/asteria/sweep/1766664321/cohort_breakdown.csv
eval-bot: Automated drift/regression check complete. Flags: recall@10 delta <= -0.03 on cohorts: short_queries, faq-anchors. Marked as "needs-triage".
arjun: Thanks. Plan suggestion: 1) baseline pipeline = normalize -> OPQ -> PQ(m=16) with ef_search=256 as default for int6. 2) For latency-critical endpoints keep int8 or float32. 3) Run targeted short-query augmentations (synthetic augment + reranking).
maya: I'll queue targeted retrain of OPQ codebooks on short-query-heavy shard and re-run fuzzcheck (random query perturbations) overnight. Also will run a small canary with concat-last4+PCA for a/b.
tom: If concat-last4 looks promising in a/b, we can consider a hybrid routing: high-value routes do concat (bigger index), default routes stay compact.
sophie: Also add a unit eval that asserts silhouette >= 0.35 for onboarding gate (for this model class). If int6 can't meet with OPQ, block int6 rollout.
arjun: Agreed. Can you create a quick PR with the eval config + the cohort CSV and the recommended default index params? I can flip the canary once PR merges.
maya: Will do — PR with config and small readme coming in ~1h. Thanks everyone :+1: 
tom: :thumbsup:
eval-bot: Schedule: nightly fuzzcheck queued (job id fj-1766664321). Results ETA ~12h.
